goal: Expose the already-implemented approve_breaking_intent_revision operation on the imm_kernel_canary tool schema so a scope change can be approved in place and execution resumed, instead of forcing the current task to stop and a successor intent to be enrolled. The Kernel side already exists end to end -- the action type in types.ts, the reducer branch in reducer_v2.ts, validation in validation.ts, the application path in application_v2.ts, and the capability action builder in canary_application.ts -- so this slice adds no new authority primitive and no new attestation. What is missing is only the tool-schema member and its dispatch in the extension, which is why the capability is unreachable from the host today. The operation is capability-bound exactly like record_user_approval, so it must reuse the existing mintCapability path and the same TUI confirmation route rather than introducing a second way to authorize a mutation. This is the highest value-to-risk slice in the roadmap and it compounds: every future slice that discovers a scope defect mid-execution becomes recoverable in place instead of being discarded and re-authored.

acceptance.assertion: The imm_kernel_canary tool schema accepts an approve_breaking_intent_revision operation and dispatches it through the existing capability-bound path, using the same mintCapability and confirmation route as record_user_approval rather than a parallel authorization mechanism.
Approving a breaking intent revision clears replan_required and lets the current task continue under its existing enrollment, with no successor TaskIntent and no second enrollment.
